summary: @servicetitan/micro-frontend ships alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload at install time
details: Package declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/` into a temp directory, extracts `bun`/`bun.exe`, marks it executable, and invokes it (`execFileSync`) against a bundled 727KB single-line obfuscated script `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a Bun-cjs bundle carrying a shuffled string-array table and rotating decoder functions (`WV8StW`, `hc1jfK9`), and is not referenced by any file under `dist/`. The package is advertised as a React micro-frontend library; neither the Bun runtime nor the obfuscated bundle relates to that purpose. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to run a shipped obfuscated blob outside Node's introspection is a supply-chain dropper pattern rather than a legitimate native-build step. The package is published under the `@servicetitan` npm scope but `repository.url` points at `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git`, which does not correspond to a public ServiceTitan product, consistent with scope impersonation or account-takeover publication.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
